questions: What specific problem or decision needs to change?
What relevant data exists today, and who owns it?
Who or what will be affected by the decision or output?
Where must a human review, approve, or override the result?
Which laws, regulations, contractual terms, or policies may apply?
What measurable outcome would demonstrate success?
What deadline or timeline pressure constrains the work?
Which existing systems, integrations, or technical constraints must the solution work with?

rules.evidence: Derived from EU AI Act screening logic — a prohibited people-affecting use case must stop before planning.

sub_recommendations: Do not build this system. Ask legal or compliance specialists whether the business need can be met in another lawful way.
warnings: Stop here. PMAID will not create a plan for a prohibited use case.
reasons: The EU AI Act screen marked this use case as prohibited.
questions: Who confirmed the use case is not misclassified?
Is there a non-prohibited reformulation of the business need?
output.suggested_non_ai: Do not proceed with this use case. Ask legal or compliance specialists for advice.

rules.evidence: Derived from solution-fit reasoning — retrieving known records is normally served more reliably by database or search technology than machine learning.

sub_recommendations: Use a database search or another standard way to find stored information.
warnings: A database search or simple rules will usually solve this more reliably than machine learning.
reasons: You need to find information that already exists.
questions: Is semantic search actually required, or is exact match enough?
output.suggested_non_ai: Use a database search or search index.

rules.evidence: Derived from automation practice — fixed low-variance steps with few exceptions are better expressed as workflow or business rules.

sub_recommendations: Automate the fixed steps with standard workflow software or business rules.
Write down the decision rules and exceptions before considering AI.
warnings: Start with standard workflow automation or business rules before considering AI.
reasons: You want software to carry out an existing manual process.
The process follows clear steps with few exceptions.
questions: Can every decision be expressed as if-then business rules today?
What exception rate would still be acceptable without ML?
output.suggested_non_ai: Use standard workflow automation or business rules for the fixed steps.

rules.evidence: Derived from model-development prerequisites — custom prediction needs suitable data or an existing trained model.

sub_recommendations: Collect suitable data or use an existing trained model before starting a custom AI project.
warnings: A prediction model cannot be built until suitable data or an existing model is available.
reasons: You do not yet have usable data.
You are not using an existing trained model.
questions: Who owns creating the first labelled dataset?
Is a vendor model with your prompts acceptable?
output.suggested_non_ai: Use standard software until suitable data is available.

rules.evidence: Derived from standard supervised learning prerequisites — labelled historical data plus a measurable outcome.

sub_recommendations: Start with a simple model using table-based data before trying more complex models.
Clearly define the result to predict and which information is available before that result happens.
warnings: Check that past examples cover the real cases you expect, are available when the prediction is made, and do not accidentally include the answer.
reasons: You need the system to predict a result or rank cases.
You have past examples showing what happened, so a model can learn from them.
questions: What is the baseline metric we are trying to beat?
Who owns the decision on what accurate enough means?
What action will the business take on a high churn score?
How many labelled examples does the ML engineer estimate are needed?

rules.evidence: Derived from document automation practice — examples or a suitable pre-trained model can support classification and structured extraction.

sub_recommendations: Add text reading, layout handling, and information extraction only where each is needed.
Send uncertain results to a person for review.
warnings: Poor scans, inconsistent layouts, or missing text may matter more than the model you choose.
reasons: You need the system to sort documents or pull information from them.
Models designed for documents can perform this type of work.
questions: What fields must be extracted with what accuracy?
Who reviews low-confidence documents?
Are source formats stable enough for layout models?

rules.evidence: Derived from generative AI use cases — creating or rewriting content requires a generative model plus quality controls and human review.

sub_recommendations: When facts matter, make the system answer from approved sources.
Require a person to review outputs that could have a serious effect.
warnings: Generated content can vary and may be wrong. Define acceptable output and require human review.
reasons: You need the system to create or rewrite content.
questions: What is an acceptable error for generated text?
Must outputs be grounded in approved sources?

rules.evidence: Derived from anomaly-detection practice — unusual activity can be identified only against an understood baseline and a managed review process.

sub_recommendations: Agree what normal activity looks like before building alerts.
Limit repeated or low-value alerts so reviewers are not overwhelmed.
warnings: People must review alerts and record which ones were useful, or the system will produce growing amounts of noise.
reasons: You need the system to flag unusual or potentially fraudulent activity.
questions: Who triages alerts and within what SLA?
What false positive rate is acceptable?

rules.evidence: Derived from optimisation practice — allocation decisions require an explicit objective and defined constraints.

sub_recommendations: Write down the goal and all fixed limits before choosing the technical approach.
warnings: Confirm the goal and limits with the business owner, or the system may optimise the wrong thing.
reasons: You need the system to choose or allocate something while following limits and business rules.
questions: What is the single objective being optimised?
Which constraints are hard versus soft?

rules.evidence: Derived from recommendation-system practice — ranking items or actions requires a relevance outcome and interaction evidence.

sub_recommendations: Agree how you will measure whether suggestions are useful before and after launch.
Decide what to suggest when a user or item has no history.
warnings: Recommendations may keep promoting what is already popular and hide useful alternatives.
reasons: You need the system to suggest items or actions.
questions: What offline metric predicts online success?
How do new users or items get ranked?

rules.evidence: Derived from hybrid automation practice — judgement-heavy exceptions may justify prediction while deterministic steps remain rules-based.

sub_recommendations: Use fixed rules for clear cases and consider a model only for cases that genuinely require judgement.
warnings: Compare AI with a simple rules-based approach and use AI only if it performs measurably better.
reasons: The process includes judgement or exceptions that simple fixed rules may not handle well.
questions: Which steps stay rules and which need prediction?

rules.evidence: Derived from discovery practice — an unclear decision or outcome requires clarification before a technical approach can be selected.

sub_recommendations: Describe the decision, users, available data, and desired result before selecting an approach.
warnings: PMAID cannot make a reliable recommendation until the problem is described more clearly.
reasons: The intended decision or outcome is not yet clear.
questions: What decision or outcome would change if this project succeeds?
output.suggested_non_ai: Pause the technology choice until the problem is clear.

rules.evidence: Derived from conservative triage practice — unmatched answers should trigger clarification rather than a confident technical recommendation.

sub_recommendations: Review the problem and available data before choosing an approach.
warnings: Review the discovery answers and add more detail before relying on this recommendation.
reasons: Your answers did not clearly match a specific project pattern.
questions: Which problem type best describes the work?
What data exists today?
